question: After persistence and process death, does the system reconstruct the same authoritative history strongly enough to produce the same justified admissibility result?
method: three genuine subprocess invocations (A build->HOLD, B reload->HOLD->RESOLVE->RELEASE, C reload->RELEASE) + corruption controls

C1_missing_provenance.detail: reconstruction accepted empty provenance; ledger repopulated with load-time bookkeeping only

receipts_vs_provenance.finding: receipt continuity is not provenance continuity; no per-event source binding in the formal provenance ledger

minimum_repair_proposed: add a provenance-presence/binding gate at the load boundary: record per-event provenance into the ProvenanceLedger at ingest/resolve, and fail closed on reload when an authority-bearing event lacks a matching authoritative provenance record; treat a missing historical scar as continuity failure
